citation.title: Selection of Appropriate Dogs to Be Therapy Dogs Using the C-BARQ
citation.authors: Sakurama M, Ito M, Nakanowataru Y, Kooriyama T

study.cbarq_version: 2020 (101 questions; analysis used 98 items meeting response-rate filters)
study.sample: Dogs that passed Hokkaido Volunteer Dog Association therapy-dog aptitude test

therapy_dog_factor_trends.factor: Fear and anxiety towards strangers, dogs, unfamiliar situations
Resource guarding-related aggression towards family dogs

items.text: Obeys a stay command immediately.
When off the leash, returns immediately when called.
Slow to learn new tricks or tasks.
items.note: Negative loading — reverse-sense item in factor

items.text: Restlessness/agitation/pacing.
Whining.
Barking.
Excessive salivation.
Chewing/scratching at doors, floor, windows, curtains, etc.
Loss of appetite
When stepped over by a member of the household.
When approached directly by an unfamiliar child while being walked or exercised on a leash.
When stared at directly by a member of the household.
When approached directly by an unfamiliar adult while being walked or exercised on a leash.
When an unfamiliar person tries to touch or pet the dog.

factors.name: Fear and anxiety towards strangers, dogs, unfamiliar situations

items.text: When approached directly by an unfamiliar male adult while away from the home.
When approached directly by an unfamiliar child while away from the home.
When an unfamiliar person tries to touch or pet the dog.
When approached directly by an unfamiliar dog of the same or larger size.
When approached directly by an unfamiliar dog of a smaller size.
When first exposed to unfamiliar situations (e.g., first car trip, first time in elevator, first visit to veterinarian, etc.).
In response to wind or wind-blown objects.
When having nails clipped by a household member.
When barked, growled, or lunged at by an unfamiliar dog.
When strangers walk past the home while the dog is in the yard.
When mailmen or other delivery workers approach the home.
Toward unfamiliar persons visiting your home.
When joggers, cyclists, roller skaters, or skateboarders pass the home while the dog is in the yard.
When an unfamiliar person approaches the owner or a member of the owner's family at home.
Toward cats, squirrels, and other animals entering its yard.
Active, energetic, always on the go.
Playful, puppyish, boisterous.
Hyperactive, restless, has trouble settling down.
When approached directly by an unfamiliar male dog while being walked or exercised on a leash.
When approached directly by an unfamiliar female dog while being walked or exercised on a leash.
When food is taken away by a member of the household.
Licks people or objects excessively.
Rolls in animal droppings or other "smelly" substances.
When visitors arrive at its home.
Just before being taken for a walk.
Just before being taken on a car trip.
When you or other members of the household come home after a brief absence.
When playing with you or other members of your household.
When the doorbell rings.
Tends to sit close to or in contact with a member of the household when that individual is sitting down.
Tends to nudge, nuzzle, or paw a member of the household for attention when that individual is sitting down.
Becomes agitated when a member of the household shows affection for another dog or animal.
Tends to follow a member of household from room to room about the house.
When approached at a favorite resting/sleeping place by another (familiar) household dog.
Towards another (familiar) dog in your household.

factors.name: Resource guarding-related aggression towards family dogs

items.text: When approached while playing with/chewing a favorite toy, bone, object, etc., by another (familiar) household dog.
When approached while eating by another (familiar) household dog.

use_in_lab: Reference norms for therapy-suitable C-BARQ profiles (Japan certified sample). Not a replacement for Serpell official subscale scoring; factor structure is study-specific (51 items → 14 named factors).
